criteria.text: Diagnosis of cystic fibrosis with a listed CFTR gating mutation or R117H.

Listed CFTR mutation confirmed by FDA-cleared testing (with bidirectional sequencing when recommended), or prescriber documentation when lab results are unavailable. R117H is included in the FDA indication.
Patient is at least 2 years old.
Kalydeco is not used concomitantly with a strong CYP3A inducer.
Kalydeco is not used concomitantly with a strong CYP3A inhibitor without dose adjustment to compensate for the interaction.
Patient is not homozygous for the F508del mutation in the CFTR gene.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Kalydeco (ivacaftor) Criteria Version 3; Last updated 5/31/2016; Approval: Committee 11/20/2015, Pulmonologist 5/31/2016; Effective 10/3/2016.

Encoded: closed CF indication, listed mutation confirmation, age ≥2, strong CYP3A inducer exclusion, strong CYP3A inhibitor dose adjustment requirement, and homozygous F508del denial. R117H testing is supported by the indication; unavailable lab results may be replaced by documentation describing how the prescriber knows the listed mutation. Documentation verification requires manual review.
Listed mutations: G551D, G1244E, G1349D, G178R, G551S, S1251N, S1255P, S549N, S549R, or R117H. Bidirectional sequencing is required when recommended by the mutation test instructions.

Reauthorization and duration (notes only): initial coverage up to 3 months. At treatment month 3, all initial criteria must still be met and prescriber follow-up by phone, email, or office visit must find no detriment or harm; approval may continue for 6 more months.

At treatment month 9, all initial criteria must still be met; submit documentation of no detriment or harm and slowed clinical decline/disease progression, clinical stabilization, or clinical improvement. Authorization may then be approved for 1 year. Renewal and duration require manual review.
Quantity limit (notes only): maximum 2 tablets or granule packets per day. Tablet: 150 mg; unit-dose granule packets: 50 mg or 75 mg. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.
Mechanism (notes only): ivacaftor potentiates CFTR channel opening to increase chloride transport at epithelial cell surfaces.
Orkambi is linked as an alternative subject to its own indication and criteria.
